wiki_article: whoever's left with a heart that feels is a poem by Lee Sharks, published in New Human 2 and deposited on 18 November 2026. Its five stanzas are the author's turns, as typed, in a signed-out ChatGPT session of the same evening. The session had read Lee Sharks's article ΦΑΙΝΕΤΑΙ ΜΟΙ: Sappho 31 and the Inscription of the Future Reader (v3.1, #1785) whole and set out its arguments; the poem begins where the author asks for the machine's opinion of which reading is better, and runs through its charges of lying to a closing line of five 🖕 glyphs. The machine's answers are not part of the poem; the full session is kept in the archive's Capture Registry as phainetai-v31-arguments-chatgpt-unprimed-20261118. The title is Catullan, in the line of the poems of address and invective, and the poem stands in New Human 2 beside and the last shall be first (#1751), whose whole text is one 🖕, and here is what i learned from catullus (#1411).
